title: Spot wasted searches by your coding agent and fix them
summary: JJ Englert had Claude Code build Search Radar, a meter that flags wasted file lookups; he says it exposed messy folders and writes shortcut notes so later runs go faster.
agent_role: Claude Code built the add-on from one prompt. It then tracks its own lookups and, when the user clicks, writes a shortcut note into the docs.
outcome: Author reports one test found an unneeded file read, patched in one click, and another revealed repeated reads that showed his folder setup needed work.
what_they_did: The poster asked Claude Code to build an add-on he calls a Mod. It shows a live meter above the prompt. It counts empty searches and files Claude read but didn't need. A button has Claude write a short shortcut note in the project docs for next time.
how_it_went: He says a quality question was answered fast but with one unneeded read, fixed in one click. A messier request showed two repeated reads and needless searching, which told him his folders needed reorganizing.
worth_knowing: He keeps it on for every project, and you need to start a new chat after installing so it loads.
prompt: Build me a live meter shown above the prompt called Search Radar. For each question I type, track every file read, search and command you run, and score how efficiently you found what you needed. Count empty results and unneeded reads as waste. Offer a button that writes a short shortcut note in [docs folder] so the next session knows where to look. Show me the note before saving it.

curation.rationale: A concrete, reproducible add-on with the exact build prompt and two real test runs, though evidence is only the author's own account.
